# Regression test for 'bolero install' locations in BOLERO_PATH mode.
env BOLERO_MODULE=off
[short] skip

# Without $BOLERO_BIN set, binaries should be installed into the BOLERO_PATH bin directory.
env BOLERO_BIN=
rm $BOLERO_PATH/bin/go-cmd-test$GOEXE
bolero install go-cmd-test
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/go-cmd-test$GOEXE

# With $BOLERO_BIN set, binaries should be installed to $BOLERO_BIN.
env BOLERO_BIN=$WORK/bin1
mkdir -p $BOLERO_BIN
bolero install go-cmd-test
exists $BOLERO_BIN/go-cmd-test$GOEXE

# Issue 11065: installing to the current directory should create an executable.
cd go-cmd-test
env BOLERO_BIN=$PWD
bolero install
exists ./go-cmd-test$GOEXE
cd ..

# Without $BOLERO_BIN set, installing a program outside $BOLERO_PATH should fail
# (there is nowhere to install it).
env BOLERO_PATH= # reset to default ($HOME/go, which does not exist)
env BOLERO_BIN=
! bolero install go-cmd-test/helloworld.go
stderr '^bolero: no install location for \.go files listed on command line \(BOLERO_BIN not set\)$'

# With $BOLERO_BIN set, should install there.
env BOLERO_BIN=$WORK/bin1
bolero install go-cmd-test/helloworld.go
exists $BOLERO_BIN/helloworld$GOEXE

# We can't assume that we can write to BOLERO_ROOT, because it may not be writable.
# However, we can check its install location using 'bolero list'.
# cmd/fix should be installed to BOLERO_ROOT/pkg, not BOLERO_PATH/bin.
env BOLERO_PATH=$PWD
bolero list -f '{{.Target}}' cmd/fix
stdout $BOLERO_ROOT'[/\\]pkg[/\\]tool[/\\]'$GOOS'_'$GOARCH'[/\\]fix'$GOEXE'$'

# BOLERO_BIN should not affect toolchain install locations.
env BOLERO_BIN=$WORK/bin1
bolero list -f '{{.Target}}' cmd/fix
stdout $BOLERO_ROOT'[/\\]pkg[/\\]tool[/\\]'$GOOS'_'$GOARCH'[/\\]fix'$GOEXE'$'

-- go-cmd-test/helloworld.go --
package main

func main() {
	println("hello world")
}
